findings.claim: userPermDenialCacheKey joins its components (action, name, parent) with '_' without escaping. UIDs can contain '_', so different (name, parent) pairs produce the same cache key, and a cached denial for one resource wrongly denies another.

verifier.reason: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 builds the key as `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` with no escaping. Grafana UIDs may contain '_', so the pair name="a", parent="b_c" and the pair name="a_b", parent="c" produce the same key. service.go:116-120 then returns Allowed:false straight from that cached entry, before any real permission check.

findings.claim: The test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' seeds permCache with false for dashboards:uid:dash1, although its comment says the entry allows access. The fallback fakeStore is empty, so the test passes even if the permDenialCache lookup is removed.

verifier.reason: service_test.go (patch lines 337-338) says the entry allows access but seeds permCache with map{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. If the permDenialCache check at service.go:117 were removed, the permCache hit would still deny: checkPermission (service.go:558) treats false as no grant, and checkInheritedPermissions finds no folder scopes, since setupService uses an empty fakeStore (service_test.go:1328). So the test does not prove that the denial cache is used.

findings.claim: Check trusts cached permission grants and returns them immediately, but ignores cached denials from the same permission cache and re-queries the DB. As a result, stale cached grants can give access to revoked resources.

verifier.reason: Cached grants were already trusted for the 30s shortCacheTTL before this patch: getUserPermissions returned permCache hits directly (removed lines at service.go ~377 in the patch). The new Check (service.go:114-127) only adds a DB re-query when the cached map does not grant access, which makes denials fresher and does not make grants staler, so the asymmetry the claim describes does not cause stale grants to give access.

findings.claim: Check returns a denial immediately from permDenialCache but ignores denials in the permission cache so that new grants are picked up. Once a denial is stored in permDenialCache, any permission granted afterward is blocked for up to the cache TTL.

verifier.reason: When the permission cache denies, Check falls through to the database (service.go, patch lines 114-128). But Check first returns a denial from permDenialCache (patch lines 107-112), and every database denial is stored there (lines 137-139) with shortCacheTTL = 30s (service.go:32). So a permission granted after a denial stays blocked for up to 30s. Before the patch, a stale permCache entry caused a similar 30s delay, so the window is bounded and no longer than before.

findings.claim: TestService_getUserPermissions no longer has a cacheHit:true case, so the cacheHit field and both 'if tc.cacheHit' branches are dead. No test asserts the always-go-to-store behavior or the removed anonymous cache read.

verifier.reason: Once the patch deletes the only `cacheHit: true` case, every case left in TestService_getUserPermissions (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:341-356) sets `cacheHit: false`. That makes the field (line 337) and both `if tc.cacheHit` branches (lines 367 and 388) dead code, and no test pre-fills the cache and then checks that getIdentityPermissions still calls the store, or that the anonymous cache read is gone (lines 841 and 1240 only check that the cache gets written). The new 'outdated cache' subtest in TestService_CacheCheck covers a stale cache falling back to the store only indirectly, through Check.

findings.claim: The denial cache key uses the raw checkReq.UserUID instead of the resolved userIdentifiers.UID used by getCachedIdentityPermissions.

verifier.reason: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 the patch builds the denial key from the raw checkReq.UserUID, while getCachedIdentityPermissions builds the permission key from the resolved userIdentifiers.UID returned by GetUserIdentifiers (service.go:452-470, which also accepts a numeric ID). The two keys are inconsistent, but each raw identifier still maps to a single user, so this only splits cache entries and should not grant the wrong access.

findings.claim: Denial cache keys share the '.perm_<uid>_' prefix with userPermCacheKey in the same cache, so the two key types can collide.

verifier.reason: Both keys do start with `<ns>.perm_<uid>_` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:26-32), but they can't realistically collide. The mapper only produces actions without underscores (mapper.go:32-41), so a permission key has one segment after the uid while a denial key always adds `_<name>_<parent>`; a match would need a user UID containing an action string and a folder UID equal to an action such as `folders:read`, and even then cacheWrap's typed JSON unmarshal (cache.go:70-74) would turn it into a cache miss, not a wrong answer.

findings.claim: getCachedIdentityPermissions returns an error that is used only as a hit/miss flag and duplicates the identity-type switch of getIdentityPermissions. Callers treat any error, including store errors and unsupported types, as a cache miss rather than only cache.ErrNotFound.

verifier.reason: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342-368, getCachedIdentityPermissions repeats the identity-type switch from getIdentityPermissions (lines 330-339). It returns the GetUserIdentifiers store error or an 'unsupported identity type' error as well as cache.ErrNotFound, and both Check (`if err == nil`) and List (`else` branch) treat any non-nil error as a cache miss and fall back to getIdentityPermissions.

findings.claim: Removing the permCache read from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions, adding a per-(user, action, name, parent) denial cache, and using NoopCache for the in-process client make DB and permission-decode load scale with the number of distinct denied resources rather than with users x actions.

verifier.reason: In service.go:113-152, any check that misses the denial cache and is not allowed by the cached map calls getIdentityPermissions. getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions (service.go:370-439) no longer read permCache, so they always query the DB, and only the denial for that one (user, action, name, parent) gets cached (cache.go:30). As a result, every distinct denied resource causes a DB fetch per TTL instead of one per user×action. The in-process client also uses NoopCache now (rbac.go:101-105), so every Check reaches the server and decodes the permissions again.

findings.claim: The denial cache key omits the identity type. Anonymous and render-service identities both have UID '0', so a cached anonymous denial also denies the render service on the same resource for the cache TTL.

verifier.reason: The denial cache key is built only from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent folder (cache.go:30-32, service.go:116). The identity type is left out. Both identities get the same UID: render.go:48-50 and anonymous client.go:115-116 set ID "0" and no UID, so `GetUID()` (identity.go:95) yields an identical userUID. An anonymous denial is cached at service.go:146-148 and then denies the render service, which should get `*` for dashboards:read (service.go:446-447), for shortCacheTTL. The reverse also happens.

findings.claim: A new exported NoopCache type in the public authz package has only one in-package call site and may duplicate functionality from authlib.

verifier.reason: The patch adds the exported `NoopCache` type in pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239-251, and it is used only once in the repository, at pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 (`authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})`). I could not check whether authlib already has an equivalent no-op cache, because the authlib module is not in the repository and I was denied access to the module cache; the claim only says it 'may' duplicate one.

findings.claim: The NoopCache methods use the receiver name 'lc' (a LocalCache abbreviation), which does not reflect the type.

verifier.reason: In change.patch lines 45-55, the patch adds `type NoopCache struct{}`, and its Get, Set and Delete methods all use the receiver `lc *NoopCache`. The name `lc` does not match the type, which would normally be named something like `nc`.

findings.claim: The newly added log message 'could not check permission' starts with a lowercase letter, which violates the convention that messages start with a capital letter.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `ctxLogger.Error("could not check permission", ...)` at pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:127, and contribute/backend/instrumentation.md:33 says log messages should start with a capital letter. The rest of this file already uses lowercase messages, including the same text at line 148, so the patch copies the file's existing style.
